summary: Lincoln County lookout: a 1931 tower, a tower moved from Little Hebo in 1958-59, and removal in 1973. No source I found describes the summit today.

facts.design: Timber tower with 7x7 ft cab (the 1958-59 tower, moved from Little Hebo)
facts.status_note: Tower taken down in 1973; no source I found describes what remains on the summit now.

events.note: Telephone line planned toward the summit, where a lookout station was to be established; the Osbornes Project gives 1915 as the first establishment, by telephone connection
Telephone line connected to the government lookout station on the summit
Fire-finding instrument sent to the station
A man was sent to the peak to locate fires
Crow's nest on the site; the register and firelookout.com date it to the 1930s only
Cabin and tower built (Osbornes Project); newspapers describe a new tower on the north side of the mountain in September 1931, at 60 ft in a late-September item and 50 ft in a June 1932 report
Kocher named as the lookout man in 1931-1932 newspaper items
100-foot tower and 16 x 22 ft ground cabin constructed, for use in the 1959 season
Tower taken down at Little Hebo, hauled to Table Mountain and reassembled; the Little Hebo register dates the move to 1959
Tower taken down; the Osbornes Project says dismantled, firelookout.com says destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe a crow's nest in the 1930s; the Osbornes Project and 1931 newspapers describe a tower built that year. The story reports both and does not choose between them.
The 1958 annual report says the replacement tower was built in 1958 for use in the 1959 season; the register gives 1959. Both fit a 1958 build with 1959 first use.
A late-September 1931 Siuslaw Oar item gives 60 feet for the tower completed on Table Mountain; the June 1932 report gives 50 feet. The story reports both.

sources.title: Table Mountain - FOREST LOOKOUTS (newspaper and Lincoln FPA annual report extracts)

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 18.3 (60 ft) does not match the sources: the 1958 annual report gives a 100-foot tower and the register 102 feet. No cab-floor height is stated, so height_m was not changed. Sources disagree on the Little Hebo tower's material (steel per the Little Hebo register, timber per the Table register and the 1958 report). Kocher name variants (Pat, H. L., 'Pap') are inferred to be one man. The story reports the 60-foot figure (Sept 1931) with the 50-foot figure (June 1932). No source describes the summit today or whether it is accessible; the access level is left unset. Unread lead: the Kemnow Online History PDF at orww.org/Osbornes_Project/Lincoln/Table_Mountain/Kemnow-Table_Mt_20200202.pdf may describe the site now. Do not confuse with the Table Mountain lookout near Mt. Shasta and Pilot Rock (cherylhill.net 2022 visit; NHLR table-mountain-lookout), which is a different site and was not used.
